title: Unique Paths
pattern: Grid DP: paths from above + paths from the left
statement: A robot starts in the top-left corner of an `m × n` grid and can only move **right or down**. How many different paths lead to the bottom-right corner?

example.why: Every path consists of 2 moves down and 3 moves right in some order: 5! / (2! · 3!) = 10.

idea: Let `dp[i][j]` be the number of paths from the start to cell `(i, j)`.
The robot can enter a cell only **from above** or **from the left**. Every path to either of those cells extends to exactly one path into this cell, so `dp[i][j] = dp[i − 1][j] + dp[i][j − 1]`.
Cells in the top row or the left column can be reached in exactly one way (straight along the edge), so they are 1.

complexity.timeWhy: Each cell is filled once with one addition.
complexity.spaceWhy: The table (a single row would be enough, since only the row above is read).

steps.text: Our example: **`m = 3, n = 4`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.

Fill the whole table with 1. For the **top row** and the **left column** that is already the final answer: there is exactly one way to get there — straight along the edge. The inner cells are computed next.
